semantic_correction.stem: An asymptomatic 32-year-old adult has obesity, is physically inactive, and has a parent with type 2 diabetes. Which action best reflects current diabetes screening guidance?

options.A: Consider testing for prediabetes or type 2 diabetes now because obesity plus additional recognized risk factors supports testing before age 35.
options.B: Wait until age 35 because screening before that age is not considered when an asymptomatic adult has additional diabetes risk factors.
options.C: Defer testing until classic hyperglycemia symptoms appear because risk-based testing is not used in asymptomatic adults.
options.D: Wait for hypertension to develop because family history and physical inactivity do not affect screening decisions.

semantic_correction.rationale: The American Diabetes Association's 2026 Standards of Care recommend assessing risk for prediabetes and type 2 diabetes in asymptomatic adults and considering testing at any age in adults with overweight or obesity who have one or more additional risk factors. Table 2.5 lists a first-degree relative with diabetes and physical inactivity among recognized risk factors. For people who do not otherwise meet risk-based criteria, screening begins at age 35. This 32-year-old therefore meets risk-based criteria for testing now rather than waiting for age 35 or symptoms.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Apply ADA risk-based diabetes screening by considering testing before age 35 when overweight or obesity is accompanied by one or more recognized diabetes risk factors.
semantic_correction.source_organization: American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee
semantic_correction.source_document_title: 2. Diagnosis and Classification of Diabetes: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026
semantic_correction.source_version_date: Diabetes Care 2026;49(Supplement 1):S27–S49; published December 8, 2025; current article accessed August 21, 2026
semantic_correction.source_locator: Recommendations 2.11 and 2.12a–2.12c; Table 2.5 — assess risk in asymptomatic adults; consider testing at any age with overweight/obesity plus one or more risk factors; risk factors include first-degree relative with diabetes and physical inactivity; for all other people screening begins at age 35
semantic_correction.source_claim_supported: ADA 2026 recommends considering testing for prediabetes or type 2 diabetes in asymptomatic adults of any age with overweight or obesity plus one or more recognized risk factors, including first-degree family history or physical inactivity; age 35 is the starting age for people who do not otherwise meet risk-based criteria.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: removed the 'only' distractor cue, changed the correct response from a categorical screening command to ADA's more precise 'consider testing' wording, and balanced alternatives around age, symptoms, and recognized risk factors.

audit_findings_append.source_authority: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026
audit_findings_append.blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance — risk-based preventive screening
audit_findings_append.finding: The revised item accurately applies ADA 2026 risk-based screening to an asymptomatic 32-year-old with obesity, physical inactivity, and first-degree family history.

option_audit.A: Correct. The client meets ADA risk-based criteria for considering testing before age 35.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Age 35 is not a minimum when overweight/obesity and additional risk factors are present.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. ADA specifically recommends risk assessment and testing in selected asymptomatic adults.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. First-degree family history and physical inactivity are recognized risk factors; hypertension is not required.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone matches the current ADA risk-based screening criteria and recommendation wording.
cueing_check: All four choices are screening decisions of comparable length and specificity; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.

checks: Recommendation 2.12a any-age risk-based testing verified directly
